Day 1Night in Tokyo
東京到着

Arrival in Tokyo

Keep this day light after the international flight.

Night in Tokyo
15–75 kmAirport to hotel
30–100 minBy private van
₹5,000–18,000Transfer for 4

Plan for the day

  1. Flight

    Your start city to Tokyo on an open-jaw ticket, arriving at Narita (NRT) or Haneda (HND). Allow for immigration, baggage and the airport transfer.

  2. Transfer

    Airport to hotel is roughly 20–75 km depending on airport and hotel area: 30–100 minutes by road, traffic dependent.

  3. Evening

    Shibuya Crossing and the Hachiko Statue if arrival time permits. Otherwise rest and eat near the hotel.

Good to know

Live weather for this day’s area loads when you’re online.

The airport transfer budget assumes one vehicle with enough luggage space. Public rail costs less but means more luggage handling and transfers.

Keep the order flexible for weather, crowd levels and your father’s walking comfort. Check opening days, timed-entry rules and transport service notices close to travel.

浅草とチームラボ

Asakusa and teamLab Planets

Traditional Tokyo in the morning, immersive art in the afternoon.

Night in Tokyo

Plan for the day

  1. Morning

    Senso-ji Temple and Nakamise Shopping Street. Allow 2–2.5 hours.

  2. Optional

    Tokyo Skytree observation deck if the group wants a paid viewpoint.

  3. Afternoon

    teamLab Planets in Toyosu. Allow around 2 hours; timed entry recommended. Some installations involve water and barefoot areas.

  4. Evening

    Dinner around Toyosu or Ginza, then back to the hotel.

Day 3Night in Tokyo
ミュージアムとパレード

Doraemon Museum and half-day Disneyland

A long day. The Disney evening parade is the priority.

Night in Tokyo
35–45 kmMuseum to Disneyland
60–90+ minRail between them
₹18,960–21,600Disney After 3 for 4

Plan for the day

  1. 09:30–12:00

    Fujiko F. Fujio Museum, Kawasaki. Advance timed-entry reservation is required; closed Tuesdays and some special dates.

  2. 12:00–14:00

    Lunch and transfer to Maihama for Tokyo Disneyland. Allow 60–90+ minutes including station changes.

  3. From 15:00

    Target an After 3 Passport if offered for the selected weekend or holiday. Check the ticket calendar for your date. Prioritise the evening Electrical Parade Dreamlights; a daytime parade is a bonus.

  4. Night

    Train back to the Tokyo hotel after the parade.

Good to know

Live weather for this day’s area loads when you’re online.

Combining the museum and Disneyland makes this day tight. The current After 3 Passport is for weekends and holidays from 3 p.m.; weekday evening tickets may start at 5 p.m. Confirm 2027 products and parade times. A half-day ticket does not guarantee a daytime parade. If the parade is non-negotiable, choose a date whose official schedule lists the evening parade and arrive early enough for a viewing spot.

Parade priority: the official show schedule comes out around the 8th of the month before your visit. The evening Electrical Parade Dreamlights is not guaranteed on every date, so book a date whose schedule lists it.

Keep the order flexible for weather, crowd levels and your father’s walking comfort. Check opening days, timed-entry rules and transport service notices close to travel.

Day 4Night in Tokyo
富士山と河口湖

Optional Mount Fuji and Lake Kawaguchi

Weather-dependent. Decide on the forecast and visibility.

Night in Tokyo
110–130 kmTokyo to the lake
9–11 hrFull day out
₹35,000–55,000Excursion for 4

Plan for the day

  1. Early start

    Tokyo to Lake Kawaguchi in the Fuji Five Lakes. Use a cancellable private van or small-group coach.

  2. Stops

    Lake Kawaguchi, Oishi Park and, if access and weather allow, the Mount Fuji 5th Station.

  3. Evening

    Back at the Tokyo hotel. This is sightseeing only, not a mountain-climbing day.

Good to know

Live weather for this day’s area loads when you’re online.

June is often cloudy or rainy around Fuji. The 5th Station can be inaccessible or unsuitable depending on weather and road operations. Keep the excursion cancellable. If visibility is poor, skip the paid tour and use this as a Tokyo flex day: a potential saving of ₹35,000–55,000 for the group.

Keep the order flexible for weather, crowd levels and your father’s walking comfort. Check opening days, timed-entry rules and transport service notices close to travel.

Tap a pin or a stop below. Use + or double-tap to zoom.

Day 5Night in Osaka
新幹線で大阪へ

Tokyo to Osaka by Shinkansen, then Osaka Castle

The bullet train is the planned intercity transfer.

Night in Osaka
552.6 kmTokyo to Shin-Osaka
~2 hr 21 minNozomi, fastest
₹34,000–38,0004 reserved seats

Plan for the day

  1. 08:00–09:00

    Hotel check-out and transfer to Tokyo Station.

  2. 09:30–12:00

    Reserved-seat Tokaido Shinkansen Nozomi to Shin-Osaka. Rail distance 552.6 km; fastest journey about 2 hr 21 min, plus practical station and boarding time.

  3. 13:00–15:30

    Transfer to the hotel, leave bags or check in, then Osaka Castle and its park.

  4. 17:00 onward

    Dotonbori and Shinsaibashi for food, a canal walk and shopping.

Good to know

Live weather for this day’s area loads when you’re online.

Four reserved ordinary seats are budgeted. JR Central publishes the Tokaido Shinkansen operating distance as 552.6 km. Oversized baggage over 160 cm total dimensions needs the appropriate seat reservation; confirm current rules before travel. Reserve four seats together.

Day 6Night in Osaka
京都 寺めぐりと竹林

Kyoto: shrine gates, temples and the bamboo grove

A full Kyoto day. Shrine and temples first, the Arashiyama bamboo grove last.

Night in Osaka
45–55 kmOsaka to Kyoto
30–45 minGion to Arashiyama
₹1,200–2,000Return rail for 4

Plan for the day

  1. 07:30–08:30

    Osaka to Kyoto. Start early to beat the busiest crowds.

  2. 09:00–10:30

    Fushimi Inari Taisha, lower torii paths.

  3. 11:00–13:00

    Kiyomizu-dera and the Sannenzaka / Ninenzaka historic lanes; lunch nearby.

  4. 13:30–14:45

    Gion district walk. Skip Nishiki Market today unless you drop the bamboo grove.

  5. 15:00–15:45

    Gion to Arashiyama: Hankyu train from Kyoto-Kawaramachi, changing at Katsura, then a 10–15 minute walk.

  6. 15:45–17:15

    Arashiyama Bamboo Grove, with Togetsukyo Bridge and the river if energy allows.

  7. Evening

    Return to Osaka by Hankyu straight from Arashiyama, about 50 minutes to Osaka-Umeda.

Good to know

Live weather for this day’s area loads when you’re online.

The bamboo grove is an addition to the original plan, which skipped Arashiyama to avoid rushing. It sits at the end of the day on purpose: if your father is tired after Gion, drop it and go back to Osaka from Gion instead. Nothing else depends on it. Times from 13:30 onward and the two added rows are new estimates.

Kyoto distances are approximate route distances; actual rail distance varies with the Osaka hotel and line chosen. Add a taxi allowance if your father prefers fewer walks and transfers.

Keep the order flexible for weather, crowd levels and your father’s walking comfort. Check opening days, timed-entry rules and transport service notices close to travel.

Tap a pin or a stop below. Use + or double-tap to zoom.

Stop 1 of 5
Fushimi Inari Taisha

A major Shinto shrine famous for thousands of vermilion torii gates winding up Mount Inari. The lower paths give a memorable visit without a full hike.

Go there nowMore photosFind on map
Stop 2 of 5
Kiyomizu-dera

A historic hillside Buddhist temple with a large wooden terrace and broad views over Kyoto. One of the city’s signature heritage sites.

Go there nowMore photosFind on map
Stop 3 of 5
Sannenzaka / Ninenzaka

Preserved sloping lanes with traditional façades, small shops and cafés. They connect the temple area with Kyoto’s historic atmosphere.

Go there nowMore photosFind on map
Stop 4 of 5
Gion

Kyoto’s historic entertainment district, known for traditional streets and teahouse architecture. Be respectful of residents and private lanes.

Go there nowMore photosFind on map
Stop 5 of 5
Arashiyama Bamboo Grove

A path through towering green bamboo in west Kyoto, one of the city’s best-known sights. It is flat and short, so it is an easy last stop; Togetsukyo Bridge and the river are a few minutes away.

Go there nowMore photosFind on map

Route in the best order

Fushimi Inari stays first to beat the crowds, the east side is walked downhill from Kiyomizu to Gion, and the bamboo grove comes last so the train home leaves straight from Arashiyama.

奈良と大阪の夜

Nara day trip and Osaka shopping

Nara in the morning, Shinsaibashi later.

35–55 minTrain each way

    Nara Park, Todaiji Temple and its Great Buddha, and optional Kasuga Taisha.

Live weather for this day’s area loads when you’re online.

Nara Park itself is free. Deer crackers are an optional small cash purchase; do not feed the deer other food. Add a modest allowance for Kasuga Taisha if entering paid areas.

Day 8Night in Osaka
ユニバーサル・スタジオ・ジャパン

Universal Studios Japan

A full day at the park. Super Nintendo World first.

Night in Osaka
10–14 kmHotel to the park
20–35 minTrain each way
₹20,160–28,560Studio Pass for 4

Plan for the day

  1. 07:30–08:30

    Osaka hotel to Universal City Station on the JR Yumesaki Line, changing at Nishikujo. Be at the gate before the posted opening time; the park often opens earlier.

  2. Opening–12:00

    Super Nintendo World first, then The Wizarding World of Harry Potter. On busy days each area needs a free timed-entry ticket, taken in the official app once you are inside.

  3. 12:00–13:00

    Lunch in the park.

  4. 13:00–18:00

    Rides and shows at your own pace. The sit-down shows give your father a rest between rides.

  5. Evening

    Stay for the lights, or leave before the closing rush. Train back to the hotel and pack for tomorrow’s flight.

Good to know

Live weather for this day’s area loads when you’re online.

This day was added to the original plan, so the trip is now nine days and the flight home moves to day 9. It needs one more hotel night in Osaka and adds roughly ₹43,000–59,000 to the budget for four.

Tickets are dated and priced by day, from ¥8,400 to ¥11,900 for an adult; weekdays are usually cheapest. A senior ticket, for ages 65 and over, starts at ¥7,600. An Express Pass, from about ¥10,800 each, is extra and only worth it on a crowded date.

Short of time? A Twilight Pass, for entry from 15:00, is sold on some dates for about ¥6,000. You could use it after Nara on day 7 and keep the trip to eight days, but that makes a long day just before the flight.

Keep the order flexible for weather, crowd levels and your father’s walking comfort. Check opening days, timed-entry rules and transport service notices close to travel.

The JR station for the park, on a short branch from Nishikujo. A street of shops and restaurants leads from the ticket gates to the park entrance, about five minutes on foot.

Universal Studios Japan

One of Japan’s biggest theme parks, on the Osaka waterfront, with areas built around films and games. Tickets are dated, so buy them before you go.

The park’s busiest area, with the Mario Kart and Yoshi rides and the Donkey Kong Country extension. Go here first; on busy days entry needs a timed ticket from the official app.

Hogwarts castle and Hogsmeade village, with the park’s best-known ride inside the castle. It is at its prettiest after dark, when the castle is lit.

Plan for the day

  1. Flight − 4 hr

  3. Departure

    KIX to your start city, direct if available on your chosen date or one-stop via a major hub.

Recommended savings target: ₹10–10.5 lakh for all four, excluding major shopping and optional upgrades. Keep another ₹30,000–50,000 for shopping or personal spending.

Hotels in the budget

Prices shown are the “from” price per room per night on booking sites, not a quote for your dates, so treat them as a guide and tap the Google button for the real figure. The budget uses the average of the picks for Lean and the dearest pick for Comfortable, plus a small allowance for hotel taxes. Type your own price to override it.

Move the slider or switch to see the estimate change. With nothing changed, Lean is ₹7,98,360 and Comfortable is ₹9,56,760. The itinerary as uploaded came to ₹7,55,400 and ₹8,97,600; the difference is the added Universal Studios day.

How it scales: flights, visas, insurance, meals, tickets and rail fares are per adult. Rooms take at most 2 adults. Private vans (airports and Mount Fuji) are counted as one per 4 adults. Hotels follow the Hotels tab: the plan’s allowance for 3-star, and the hotel picks for 4-star unless you choose otherwise.

say

Voice

The voice comes from your device, so Kon can only sound as good as the Japanese voice installed there. Mac: Apple menu, System Settings, Accessibility, Spoken Content (called Read & Speak on newer versions), then the System voice menu and Manage Voices. Find Japanese, download Kyoko, then quit and reopen the browser. iPhone or iPad: Settings, Accessibility, Spoken Content, Voices, Japanese. Windows: Microsoft Edge has natural Japanese voices built in.

No Japanese voice on this device yet, so no audio. The beat boxes and the “say” line show how it sounds.
